stem: Best guess: what is the main tax advantage of filing a consolidated return?

choices.text: A lower corporate tax rate for the group
One member's losses offset another's income
choices.explanation: Correct. Offsetting members' income and losses is the main benefit.

choices.text: No need to file any Form 1120

explanation: Offsetting members' income and losses is the main benefit.

stem: P owns 70% of S1's voting stock and value. P also owns 50% of S2, and S1 owns 40% of S2. Which corporations are in P's affiliated group?

choices.explanation: Correct. S1 fails the 80% test, so S1's 40% of S2 doesn't count toward members' ownership; P owns only 50% of S2.

explanation: S1 fails the 80% test, so S1's 40% of S2 doesn't count toward members' ownership; P owns only 50% of S2.

stem: In a consolidated group, a 100%-owned subsidiary pays a $500,000 dividend to its parent. What is the effect on consolidated taxable income?

choices.text: No effect; the dividend is eliminated
choices.explanation: Correct. Intercompany distributions are excluded from consolidated income.
Intercompany dividends are eliminated rather than deducted.

explanation: Intercompany distributions are excluded from consolidated income.

stem: Which corporation can be included in a consolidated group?

choices.text: A foreign subsidiary 100% owned by a U.S. parent
An S corporation 100% owned by the parent
A domestic C corporation 85% owned (vote and value)
choices.explanation: Correct. Includible corporations meeting the 80% vote-and-value test join the group.

choices.text: A tax-exempt organization controlled by the parent

explanation: Includible corporations meeting the 80% vote-and-value test join the group.

stem: Which forms are filed with the first consolidated return?

choices.explanation: Correct. Form 851 lists affiliations; Form 1122 is each subsidiary's consent.

explanation: Form 851 lists affiliations; Form 1122 is each subsidiary's consent.

stem: Parent has taxable income of $900,000. Sub A (100% owned) has a $300,000 loss; Sub B (90% owned) has taxable income of $100,000. What is consolidated taxable income (no intercompany items)?
explanation: Members' separate taxable incomes are combined in full, regardless of minority interests.

stem: Sub sells inventory to Parent at a $40,000 profit in 2025. Parent still holds the inventory at year-end. How much of the profit is in 2025 consolidated taxable income?

choices.explanation: Correct. Intercompany gain is taken into account when the item leaves the group.

explanation: Intercompany gain is taken into account when the item leaves the group.

stem: What is a disadvantage of filing consolidated returns?

choices.text: Members' losses can't offset other members' income
Losses on intercompany sales are deferred
choices.explanation: Correct. Deferral works both ways: intercompany losses are deferred too, and the election is binding.

choices.text: Each member must pay separate estimated tax
choices.explanation: The group pays estimates on a consolidated basis.

explanation: Deferral works both ways: intercompany losses are deferred too, and the election is binding.

stem: A subsidiary uses a June 30 year-end; the parent uses December 31. If they file a consolidated return, which year-end applies?

choices.explanation: Members must use the parent's year.

choices.text: Whichever year produces less total tax

choices.explanation: Correct. Members use the parent's year.

explanation: Reg. §1.1502-76: each member adopts the common parent's tax year.

stem: A corporation joins a consolidated group with a $500,000 NOL from before it joined. What limits the group's use of this NOL?

choices.text: Nothing, because group NOLs are fully shareable
The at-risk rules for the members
choices.explanation: Those apply to individuals and closely held corporations for activities.

choices.text: The separate return limitation year (SRLY) rules
choices.explanation: Correct. SRLY rules (and §382 after an ownership change) limit use of losses the member brought in.

choices.text: The NOL is forfeited when it joins
choices.explanation: It can be used, subject to limits.

explanation: SRLY rules (and §382 after an ownership change) limit use of losses the member brought in.

stem: Two brother-sister corporations are each 100% owned by the same individual. Can they file a consolidated return?

choices.text: Yes, because they are commonly controlled
choices.explanation: A common corporate parent is required.

choices.text: Only if both are S corporations
Yes, if they elect with Form 1122
choices.explanation: The group still needs a corporate parent.

choices.text: No, because there is no common parent corporation
choices.explanation: Correct. An affiliated group requires an includible corporation as the common parent.

explanation: An affiliated group requires an includible corporation as the common parent.

stem: Parent (100% owner) sells equipment with a basis of $70,000 to Sub for $50,000. Sub uses the equipment in its business. How is Parent's $20,000 loss treated in the consolidated return?

choices.text: Deferred; recognized as Sub depreciates or sells
choices.explanation: Correct. Under the matching rule, the deferred loss is taken into account as the buyer's corresponding items occur.

explanation: Under the matching rule, the deferred loss is taken into account as the buyer's corresponding items occur.

stem: For 2025, a consolidated group's combined taxable income before charitable contributions is $2,000,000. The members gave $250,000 to charity in total. What is the consolidated charitable deduction?

choices.explanation: Applies 10% to the contributions instead of taxable income.
Correct. The 10% limit applies to consolidated taxable income; $50,000 carries forward.

explanation: The 10% limit applies to consolidated taxable income; $50,000 carries forward.

stem: Parent owns 85% of Sub's voting power but only 75% of its value. Can Sub join Parent's consolidated return?

choices.explanation: Correct. Both vote and value must be at least 80%.

explanation: Affiliation requires ownership of at least 80% of both total voting power and total value.

stem: How are dividends paid by a subsidiary to its parent treated in a consolidated return?
explanation: Intercompany distributions within a consolidated group are excluded from income.

stem: In a consolidated group, Sub A has a $50,000 capital gain and Sub B has a $30,000 capital loss. What is reported?

choices.explanation: Correct. Capital items net on a consolidated basis.

explanation: Consolidated capital gain net income is computed for the group, so one member's capital losses offset another's gains.

stem: Once a group elects to file consolidated returns, how long must it continue?

choices.text: Until the IRS allows a stop
choices.explanation: Correct. Unless the group ceases to exist.

choices.text: It may stop at any time it wants

explanation: A consolidated election continues for later years unless the IRS consents to discontinue or the group terminates.

stem: Parent's basis in Sub's stock is $500,000. Sub has $100,000 of taxable income (ignore taxes) and pays Parent a $30,000 dividend. What is Parent's basis after the year?
explanation: Consolidated investment adjustments increase the parent's basis for Sub's income and decrease it for distributions.

stem: Parent sells land to Sub at a $100,000 gain. Two years later Sub sells it to an outsider for $30,000 more than it paid. What does the group recognize then?

choices.explanation: The deferred gain is also recognized.
Correct. The deferred gain and Sub's gain.

explanation: Intercompany gain is deferred until the property leaves the group; then both the deferred and new gain are recognized.

stem: Who acts as agent for a consolidated group in dealing with the IRS?

choices.explanation: That isn't what the rule says.
That isn't what the rule says.
Correct. It files and communicates for the group.

explanation: The common parent is the agent for all group members on tax matters.

stem: A consolidated group can't pay its tax. Who is liable?

choices.explanation: Correct. Each member is liable for the full tax.

choices.text: No one, until a court rules

explanation: Each member of a consolidated group is severally liable for the group's consolidated tax.

stem: A subsidiary with a deferred intercompany gain on assets bought from Parent leaves the consolidated group. What happens to the deferred gain?

choices.text: It's triggered when the sub leaves

explanation: Deferred intercompany items are taken into account when a member leaves the group.

stem: A parent owns 85% of a subsidiary, and they file separate returns. What DRD applies to dividends the sub pays the parent?

choices.explanation: Correct. Members of an affiliated group qualify.

explanation: Dividends between members of an affiliated group (80%+ ownership) qualify for a 100% DRD even on separate returns.

stem: In a consolidated group, taxable income before charitable deductions is: Parent $500,000; Sub 1 $200,000; Sub 2 $(100,000). Parent gave $40,000 and Sub 1 $30,000 to charity. What is the consolidated charitable deduction?

choices.explanation: The 10% limit applies to the group.
Sub 2's loss counts in the base.
Correct. 10% of consolidated taxable income of $600,000; $10,000 carries forward.

explanation: The charitable limit is computed on consolidated taxable income.

stem: Parent sells equipment (basis $60,000) to Sub for $100,000. Sub depreciates it straight-line over 5 years. How much of Parent's deferred gain is taken into account in the first full year?

choices.explanation: The gain is matched to depreciation.
Correct. The $40,000 gain is recognized as Sub's extra depreciation is claimed: 40,000 ÷ 5.

explanation: Under the matching rule, intercompany gain is taken into account as the buyer's additional depreciation is deducted.

stem: A corporation joins a consolidated group on July 1. How is its income for the year reported?

choices.explanation: Correct. Income after joining is consolidated.

choices.text: All of it in the consolidated return
All of it on a separate return

explanation: A new member files a short separate return for the period before joining.

stem: What ownership must a parent have in a subsidiary to file a consolidated return?

choices.explanation: Correct. Both tests must be met.

explanation: An affiliated group requires 80% of total voting power and 80% of total value.

stem: In the first consolidated return year, what must each subsidiary file?

choices.explanation: Correct. Its consent to be included.

explanation: Each subsidiary consents on Form 1122 in the first consolidated return year.

stem: Which corporation may not join a consolidated return?

choices.explanation: Correct. Only includible corporations may join.

explanation: Foreign corporations, S corporations and exempt organizations aren't includible corporations.

stem: S sells land (basis $100,000) to fellow member B for $150,000. B later sells it outside the group for $170,000. What gain is recognized then?

choices.explanation: S's deferred gain is also triggered.

explanation: Intercompany gain is deferred and recognized when the property leaves the group.

stem: S sells equipment (basis $60,000) to B for $100,000. B depreciates it straight-line over 5 years. How much of S's gain is recognized each year?

choices.explanation: Correct. It matches B's extra depreciation.

explanation: Under the matching rule, S takes its gain into account as B depreciates the stepped-up basis.

stem: Consolidated taxable income before the charitable deduction is $2,000,000, and contributions total $250,000. What is deductible?

choices.explanation: It's computed on a consolidated basis.

explanation: The charitable limit is applied to consolidated taxable income.

stem: A subsidiary pays a $100,000 dividend to its parent in the same consolidated group. What is included in consolidated income?
explanation: Intercompany distributions are excluded from consolidated income.

stem: P has a $40,000 capital gain, and S (same group) has a $30,000 capital loss. What is the group's net capital gain?
explanation: Capital gains and losses are netted on a consolidated basis.

stem: S has $100,000 of income and distributes $30,000 to P. What is the net adjustment to P's basis in S?
explanation: Investment adjustments increase basis for the subsidiary's income and decrease it for distributions.

stem: S joined the group with a $200,000 SRLY NOL. S contributes $60,000 to consolidated taxable income. Ignoring the 80% limit and §382, how much NOL can be used?
explanation: SRLY losses are limited to the member's cumulative contribution to consolidated taxable income.

stem: After an ownership change, a loss corporation is worth $5,000,000, and the long-term tax-exempt rate is 3.5%. What is the annual §382 limit?
explanation: The §382 limit equals the loss corporation's value times the long-term tax-exempt rate.

stem: P's basis in S is $50,000. S's losses used by the group total $80,000. What is P's excess loss account?
explanation: Negative basis from investment adjustments is an excess loss account.

stem: Group taxable income is $500,000, and a $400,000 post-2017 consolidated NOL carryforward exists. What NOL deduction applies?
explanation: The 80% limit applies to consolidated taxable income.

stem: P acquires 100% of S on June 30. Which of S's income is included in the consolidated return?

choices.text: All of S's income for the year

choices.explanation: Correct. From the day after acquisition.

explanation: A new member's income is included starting the day after it joins the group.

stem: S has a fiscal year ending June 30, and its parent uses the calendar year. What year does S use after joining?

choices.explanation: Correct. Members use the parent's year.

explanation: All members must adopt the common parent's tax year.

stem: P has a profitable subsidiary and a loss-making subsidiary. What is a key benefit of consolidation?

choices.text: No tax on intercompany sales ever

explanation: Consolidation lets one member's losses offset another member's income immediately.

stem: What is a key drawback of electing to file consolidated returns?
explanation: Once elected, consolidated filing continues unless the IRS grants permission or the group ends.

stem: P considers selling property to S within the group to step up its basis for depreciation. Why is the benefit limited?

choices.text: The sale is void for tax

choices.explanation: Correct. The net effect is neutral.

explanation: The matching rule offsets added depreciation with recognition of the intercompany gain.

stem: A group plans to buy a company with large NOLs. What must it evaluate?

choices.explanation: Correct. Value × rate limits annual use.

explanation: An ownership change triggers the §382 annual limit, and SRLY rules may also apply.

stem: A subsidiary with a $30,000 excess loss account is sold outside the group. What happens?

choices.explanation: Correct. The negative basis is recaptured.
It is income, not a loss.

explanation: An excess loss account is included in the parent's income when the subsidiary leaves the group.

stem: An individual owns 100% of two corporations. Can they file a consolidated return?
explanation: A consolidated group needs a common corporate parent owning 80% of the others.
